_comment: Numbers the page renders. Upload a new copy of this file and the page
updates — no HTML change, no redeploy of anything else.
`decode` is a best recorded rate on that machine, or null for 'not
measured'. Null renders as 'not measured' rather than a blank or a zero,
because a missing measurement and a slow one are different claims.
`modes` is how the model runs there: gpu = fully resident, ssd = experts
stream from disk, hyb = split CPU/GPU. Several modes means the app can
use any of them; an empty list renders 'does not fit'.
_provenance: The M4 mini and DGX Spark rows were measured directly on those machines in August 2026 and carry the method in their notes. On 12 August 2026 three M1 Ultra rows were re-measured the same way and now carry medians with spreads: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Laguna-S-2.1 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Where a re-measurement moved a number it is recorded here rather than silently overwritten: Laguna-S-2.1 30.8 -> 33.4 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash 27.5 -> 28.0 (both faster than published), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 73.7 -> 72.3. The M1 Ultra DeepSeek-V4-Flash size was corrected from 97.6 GB to 87 GB: the old figure matched no file on the machine and disagreed with the same model's own M2 Max and DGX Spark rows. A fourth attempt, M2 Max Qwen3-4B, was WITHDRAWN rather than published: two runs of the identical script disagreed by 1.7x, so that row is now null. TWO LIMITS THIS EXERCISE EXPOSED, which apply to every row on this page. First, decode is not a single rate: measured on M2 Max, the 1->129 token slope and the 129->513 slope differ by 15%, because attention costs more as the context grows -- so any figure here depends on the token count it was taken at, which is 129. Second, these machines are shared, and a busy machine can halve the number; spreads are quoted so a reader can see when that happened. The remaining M1 Ultra and M2 Max rows are still carried over verbatim from the first version of this page and have NOT been re-verified. Prices are approximate street or list prices in August 2026, recorded so a rate can be read against what the machine costs -- they move, and they are not quotes. Muse Glimmer 30B was ADDED to the M1 Ultra box after the 12 August exercise and does not share its method: the figure is llama.cpp's llama-bench tg128 (build b10360), an instrument that reports a mean over repetitions rather than the median-of-paired-estimates used elsewhere on this page, so it is not strictly comparable with the rows above it and the note says so. Two figures for this model exist in our own records and are both kept rather than one being chosen silently: tg128 23.20 tok/s and tg64 ~28.9 tok/s. tg128 is published because the rest of the column is quoted at 129 generated tokens; the tg64 figure is not wrong, it is a shorter generation, which this page already records as producing a higher rate. The tg64 run is documented as having the ds4 Q4_K kernel substitution active; the tg128 run does not say, which is why the note declines to attribute the published number to an engine the way the neighbouring rows do.

boxes.label: M1 Ultra · 64-core GPU · 128 GB
boxes.price: from $3,999 at launch · discontinued, used market
boxes.note: Three of these six rows were re-measured on this machine on 12 August 2026; the figure is the median of paired estimates, not a best-ever run. Decode is isolated as the difference between a 129-token and a 1-token completion so prefill is excluded, and repetitions alternate A/B/B/A so drift lands on both arms. Each model runs on the engine the app picks for it, and they are not the same engine: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on llama.cpp with the ds4 kernels — 72.3, ten estimates spanning 67.5–78.0; Laguna-S-2.1 on the ds4 reference engine — 33.4, eight estimates spanning 33.1–34.3; DeepSeek-V4-Flash on our own Rust/Metal engine — 28.0, eight estimates spanning 27.8–28.2. The machine was shared with other work throughout, which is why the Qwen3.6 spread is the wide one; the DeepSeek figure independently reproduces a 27.9–28.2 anchor measured by a different harness. The last two rows are out-of-core rates and are still carried over unverified: GLM-5.2 is not present on this machine at all, and Kimi-K3 is present but its streaming mode is the untested claim — one attempt at an out-of-core model of that class drove the machine into 42 GB of swap and was stopped. Muse Glimmer 30B is the one row here measured by a different instrument, and is marked so rather than blended in: it is llama.cpp's own llama-bench (build b10360) reporting tg128 — 23.2 tok/s, alongside a pp512 prefill of 247.6 tok/s — not the paired A/B/B/A difference the rows above use, and not a median of paired estimates. It is quoted at 128 generated tokens because that is nearest the 129 the other rows use; the same model on the same machine was separately recorded at ~28.9 tok/s on tg64, and that 1.25× gap between 64 and 128 tokens is the same context effect noted below, not a contradiction. Which of the two Q4_K matvec paths that run used is not recorded, so unlike the rows above this one cannot be attributed to a specific set of kernels.

boxes.label: M2 Max · 64 GB
boxes.note: The same catalogue, scored for 64 GB. Qwen3-4B was measured twice here on 12 August 2026 and the two runs disagreed by 1.7× — 43.4 tok/s and then 74.9 tok/s from the identical script, model and engine. The first run was taken minutes after a 2.3 GB file landed on the machine, so the machine's state rather than the model dominated it. The row is therefore withdrawn rather than published at either figure: a number that does not mean what it says is worse than an admitted gap. It will return when it can be measured on a quiescent machine. The other three rows are still carried over from the first version of this page and have not been re-verified — this machine currently has 27 GB of disk free, so the 22 GB Qwen3.6 and the 48 GB Laguna-S cannot be stored without freeing space, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 87 GB is out-of-core here, which is what the 2.9 would cost.

boxes.label: M4 mini · 16 GB
boxes.note: A 16 GB machine is offered the models that suit it, not the whole catalogue. Both rows were re-measured on this machine in August 2026, decode isolated as the difference between a 129-token and a 1-token completion so that prefill is excluded. The larger Qwen3 variants are absent because they cannot be tested here rather than because they are slow: 14B needs a download this machine has no room for, and 32B is a 20 GB file on a 16 GB machine with 12.7 GB free — it cannot be stored, let alone run.

boxes.label: DGX Spark · GB10 · 128 GB
boxes.note: Not a Local Mind machine — the app is macOS only. This is the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash file on an NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell desktop through the reference CUDA engine, so the model and the quantisation are comparable to the Mac rows even though the engine is not. Measured August 2026 as an A/B/B/A sequence, three repetitions per arm, GPU clock sampled throughout (2405–2535 MHz); the repetitions spanned 0.06 tok/s. The weights sit in unified memory rather than streaming, which is why an 87 GB model reports a resident rate on a 128 GB box.
